1. Plan your menu based on seasonal and local ingredients. This will help you to avoid buying ingredients that are out of season or hard to come by, which can lead to waste.
2. Use all parts of the ingredients you buy. For example, use the stems of broccoli in stir-fries or chop up carrot tops to make pesto.
3. Compost any food waste you can't use. This can be done by setting up a compost bin in your kitchen and composting any food scraps that can't be used.
4. Donate any excess food to local food banks or shelters. This is a great way to use up any extra food that you can't use in your restaurant.
5. Use leftovers to create new dishes. If you have leftover ingredients from a previous meal, try using them to create a new dish. This will help you to use up any extra ingredients and create new menu items.
6. Implement a "first out, first in" policy. This means that any ingredients that have been sitting in your fridge or pantry for the longest time should be used first. This will help you to avoid wasting ingredients that have been sitting around for too long.
7. Train your staff on reducing food waste. Make sure your staff are aware of the importance of reducing food waste and are trained on how to do so. This can include things like proper portioning and portion control, using leftovers, and composting food waste.
8. Use upcycle strategies. This means using ingredients that would normally be discarded, such as trimmings, peels, and rinds, to create new dishes. For example, you could use carrot peels to make carrot top pesto or use potato skins to make potato skins with toppings.
9. Use technology to track and manage food waste. There are many software and apps available that can help you track and manage your food waste. This can help you identify areas where you can reduce waste and make informed decisions about your menu and inventory.

To implement PBL effectively, it is important to first identify a problem that your students are interested in and can relate to. Be sure to provide students with clear instructions and ample time to research and collaborate on their projects.

2. Provide clear instructions and ample time for students to research and collaborate.

5. Celebrate students' successes and encourage them to continue learning.
